sections.heading: C - Section Twelve: Driver Safety
sections.markdown:
## C - Section Twelve: Driver Safety

FACT_ID: sec12-F01 | anchor: A01
Every driver eventually assesses personal driving skill; the concerned recruit a trusted licensed observer to note dangerous behaviors and suggest fixes, listen and apply the feedback, or take professional lessons instead [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec12-F02 | anchor: A01
The Vehicle Code lets DMV investigate and reexamine any driver's safe-operation ability on the basis of physical or mental conditions or poor records, never age alone [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec12-F03 | anchor: A01
Physicians, law enforcement, and family members refer drivers with physical or mental conditions by submitting a completed Request for Driver Reexamination, form DS 699 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec12-F04 | anchor: A01
Cognitive disorders from dementia and seizures through brain tumors, Parkinson's, strokes, and vertigo threaten safe driving and can end it; mild-impairment referrals trigger Driver Safety reexaminations detailed at dmv.ca.gov/reexamination [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec12-F05 | anchor: A01
DMV reexaminations may request medical information, run in-person or telephone reviews, require knowledge, vision, or driving tests, issue limited-term licenses, immediately suspend or revoke privileges for immediate public threats, or take no action [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec12-F06 | anchor: A02
Drivers handed a Notice of Priority Reexamination with the top box checked hold five working days to contact DMV and start the process before automatic suspension [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec12-F07 | anchor: A02
Priority notices rest on incapacity evidence at a Vehicle Code violation suggesting the driver cannot operate without danger; drivers receive copies while officers fax and mail the notice to the Driver Safety Office [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec12-F08 | anchor: A02
Non-compliance notices order DMV contact under Vehicle Code sections 12818 and 12819, with missed five-working-day windows suspending driving until a satisfactory reexamination [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec12-F09 | anchor: A02
License restrictions keep drivers operating within their abilities, imposed by DMV or required by law, always reasonable and necessary, and always rooted in examiner findings and recommendations [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec12-F10 | anchor: A02
Restrictions may demand vehicle devices like hand controls, time-and-place limits like no night or freeway driving, eyeglasses or corrective contacts, or added equipment like outside mirrors [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec12-F11 | anchor: A02
No restrictions target seniors specifically; every restriction answers a condition, never an age [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0087]
